items.prompt: Where is Anna? — She ___ lunch at the moment.
items.explanation: 'At the moment' signals a temporary action now, so the present continuous 'is having' fits.

items.prompt: Yesterday we ___ to the beach.
items.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished time in the past, so the past simple 'went' is correct.

items.prompt: This city is ___ than my hometown.
items.explanation: Short adjectives form the comparative with -er: 'bigger'.

items.prompt: Look at those dark clouds — it ___ rain. (two words)
items.explanation: A present sign predicts the future, so 'is going to' is the natural choice.

items.prompt: Could I have ___ water, please?
items.explanation: 'Water' is uncountable; 'some' is used in offers and requests.

items.prompt: There is a pharmacy ___ the corner of the street.
items.explanation: 'On the corner' is the standard phrase for a position at the intersection of streets.

items.prompt: My brother ___ to work by bus every day.
items.explanation: A routine ('every day') with a third-person subject takes the present simple: 'goes'.

items.prompt: I bought ___ new phone yesterday.
items.explanation: 'A' introduces a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time.

items.prompt: This umbrella is ___ — it belongs to Sarah.
items.explanation: The possessive form of a name is noun + 's': 'Sarah's'.

items.prompt: There ___ two books on the shelf. (one word)
items.explanation: 'Two books' is plural, so the plural form 'are' is required.

items.prompt: The meeting starts ___ 9 o'clock.
items.explanation: Times use the preposition 'at': 'at 9 o'clock'.

items.prompt: ___ you like coffee?
items.explanation: Yes/no questions in the present simple use the auxiliary 'do' (with 'you').

items.prompt: I ___ never been to Japan, but I hope to go one day.
items.explanation: 'Never' with a lifetime experience takes the present perfect: 'have never been'.

items.prompt: If I ___ rich, I would travel around the world.
items.explanation: The second conditional (hypothetical) uses 'if + past' — 'were' for all persons.

items.prompt: You ___ smoke in the building — it is not allowed.
items.explanation: 'Mustn't' expresses prohibition: it is not allowed.

items.prompt: She said, 'I am tired.' → She said that she ___ tired. (one word)
items.explanation: Backshift takes the present 'am' to the past 'was' in reported speech.

items.prompt: I will look ___ the meaning of this word in the dictionary.
items.explanation: 'Look up' means to find information, e.g. in a dictionary.

items.prompt: When I was five, I ___ swim across the pool.
items.explanation: Past ability is expressed with 'could'.

items.prompt: I ___ TV when the phone rang.
items.explanation: An action in progress in the past takes the past continuous: 'was watching'.

items.prompt: The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.
items.explanation: 'Who' refers to people as the subject of a defining relative clause.

items.prompt: Look at the timetable — the train ___ at 6 p.m.
items.explanation: Fixed schedules and timetables use the present simple: 'the train leaves'.

items.prompt: You look tired — you ___ go to bed early tonight. (one word)
items.explanation: 'Should' is the natural modal for giving advice.

items.prompt: It was the ___ day of my life.
items.explanation: 'The best' is the superlative of 'good'.

items.prompt: She is good ___ solving problems.
items.explanation: 'Good at' is the fixed adjective + preposition combination.

items.prompt: The new policy ___ by the board last Monday.
items.explanation: The subject receives the action in a finished past situation, so the past passive 'was approved'.

items.prompt: If you had told me earlier, I ___ the meeting.
items.explanation: The third conditional about a past unreal situation uses 'would have + past participle'.

items.prompt: The man ___ car was stolen called the police. (one word)
items.explanation: 'Whose' expresses possession for people and things in relative clauses.

items.prompt: By this time next year, we ___ the project for ten years.
items.explanation: 'By this time next year' marks completion before a future point — the future perfect.

items.prompt: The lights are on, so they ___ home already.
items.explanation: A confident deduction about a past event uses 'must have + past participle'.

items.prompt: The plan is risky. ___, the potential reward is enormous.
items.explanation: 'However' introduces a contrast between the risk and the reward.

items.prompt: He said he ___ the report by Friday.
items.explanation: Reported speech backshifts 'will finish' to 'would finish'.

items.prompt: She ___ be at home — her lights are off.
items.explanation: 'Can't' expresses a confident negative deduction about the present.

items.prompt: The meeting was called ___ at the last minute. (one word)
items.explanation: 'Called off' means cancelled.

items.prompt: I don't mind ___ the dishes.
items.explanation: 'Mind' is followed by a gerund: 'mind doing'.

items.prompt: It was raining heavily, ___ the match was postponed.
items.explanation: 'So' introduces a result that follows from the reason.

items.prompt: This time tomorrow, I ___ on the beach.
items.explanation: An action in progress at a future moment takes the future continuous.

items.prompt: ___ was the lack of funding that stopped the project.
items.explanation: The it-cleft 'It was X that…' focuses on a specific element of the sentence.

items.prompt: ___ from the top of the hill, the town looked tiny. (one word)
items.explanation: The past participle 'Seen' introduces a passive participial clause with a shared subject.

items.prompt: You ___ told me about the delay earlier — I wasted a whole afternoon.
items.explanation: 'Shouldn't have done' expresses criticism about a past action.

items.prompt: Which sentence sounds most cautious and professional?
options: The data proves the theory wrong.
The data appears to challenge the theory.
items.explanation: 'Appears to challenge' hedges the claim, which is the cautious, register-appropriate choice.

items.prompt: ___ had we left the house when it started to pour. (two words)
items.explanation: Negative adverbials like 'no sooner' trigger inversion of subject and auxiliary.

items.prompt: The team reached a ___ consensus after hours of negotiation.
items.explanation: 'Broad consensus' is the natural, established collocation.

items.prompt: Hardly ___ we arrived when the phone rang. (one word)
items.explanation: With 'hardly' the subject and auxiliary invert, giving 'hardly had we arrived'.

items.prompt: It is essential that every student ___ the safety rules.
items.explanation: The subjunctive after 'it is essential that' uses the bare infinitive: 'obey'.

items.prompt: He let the cat out of the ___ when he mentioned the surprise.
items.explanation: 'Let the cat out of the bag' means to reveal a secret by accident.

items.prompt: The new law met with ___ opposition from local businesses. (one word)
items.explanation: 'Stiff opposition' is the strong, established collocation.

items.prompt: ___ a remarkable achievement it was!
items.explanation: Exclamations with a noun phrase use 'what': 'What a remarkable achievement'.

items.prompt: They ___ have finished by now — there's no sign of them.
items.explanation: 'Can't have done' expresses a confident negative deduction about the past.
